record.question: In the Massachusetts PRIM Board's October 2023 RFP for Multi-Asset Credit investment management services, what minimum total firm assets under management must a respondent have?
record.answer:
# Markdown Briefing

## Answer
The minimum **total firm assets under management** required is **$10 billion**.

## Supporting Details
- This requirement appears in **Section VI, “Minimum Qualifications,” item 4** of the Massachusetts PRIM Board’s **October 2023 RFP** for **Multi-Asset Credit investment management services**.
- The AUM measurement date is **September 30, 2023**.
- The RFP also notes an **alternative qualification**: at least **$2 billion in multi-asset credit strategy AUM**.

## Conclusion
For the specific question about **minimum total firm AUM**, the required threshold is **$10 billion**.

7. A description of your insurance coverages including Errors and Omissions, D&O, Fiduciary 
Liability, including names of carriers and limits; 
8. Your privacy policy with regard to sharing client and account information to outside parties;

9. A description of your data security policies and procedures, including those related to physical 
access, data encryption, back-ups, and disaster recovery; 
10. A list and description of any current or pending administrative or similar actions against you or 
your firm or an affirmative statement that there are none; 
11. A full and complete description of the process(es) by which you address participant requests for 
support, e.g., telephone-based response, web portal, and a description of what individual(s) at your 
firm will be available to participants; 
12. Description of how you assist with new enrollee procedures including whether you will provide 
representatives for on-site enrollment and other educational meetings; 
13. A description of participant statements and whether they can be customized. Include samples and 
specify whether personalized rates of return are included; 
14. A description of your quality standards related to returning requests for administration assistance 
from your clients; 
15. A full and complete description of the services you will and will not provide for each of the items 
listed under “Scope of Work” above. Include your fee structure, consultant hourly rates and/or 
other pricing arrangements for annual plan administration fees itemized by base fees, if applicable, 
and/or per participant fees. Also, describe any 12b-1 fees, commissions, rebates, asset-based 
fees,or other compensation received by you, your employees, or firm or a related/affiliated broker 
or other similar entity for any mutual funds that will be contained in our plans; 
16. A full and complete description of any fees, commissions, revenue-sharing arrangements, 
commission recapture, or similar arrangements that are received by you, your employees, or firm 
from any related/affiliated entity associated with the servicing of our plans, but received from 
sources other than our plans; 
17. A description of all the types of plan documents you provide and support (standardized and non-standardized prototype plans, volume submitter, individually designed) and a list of potential plan 
custodians for each of these products; 
18. A specimen copy of your client service agreement, contract, or other relevant document; 
19. Description of fund and fund family offerings included in your fee quote and any variations 
thereof, including maximum number of funds provided and any limitations on the number of 
funds or families offered within the total offering. Also specify whether it is possible to invest in 
funds not managed by your company or the custodian(s) with which you are affiliated; 
20. A description of what information you will provide regarding funds and fund options; provide 
specimen copies of this material; 
21. A description and/or samples of plan management reports that include total assets, contributions, 
and other statistics and whether that information is available on a plan sponsor website; 
22. A copy of your latest SAS #70 Service Organization Report or a statement that you do not have 
one; 
23. References for five not-for-profit organization clients with budgets in the range of $5M to $15M 
including organization name, contact; phone number and email, number of years as administrator, 
and number of participants.

American Academy of Actuaries – Retirement Plan Services Page 6

All information presented during the proposal process is confidential.

Proposals are due by May 31, 2011 and should be sent to Steve Knell at the contact information noted

Services by 4:00 P.M. on Thursday, August 31, 2023.

of Grand Rapids Police and Fire Retirement System (collectively the “Board”) are in the 
process of reviewing their investment consultant services. The purpose of this RFP is to 
gain adequate information from which the Boards may evaluate such services. This RFP 
includes detail on general (non-discretionary) and discretionary (OCIO) services. Firms are 
asked to submit proposals for either, or both, as appropriate. 
Further information about the Plan is available at https://grpensions.org/.

approximately $437 Million as of June 30, 2023.

global equity; 8% non-U.S. equity; 8% ADRs; 8% private equity; 5% treasury inflation-protected securities; 5% real estate (REITs); 5% commodities; 5% mid-stream energy; and

advice and counsel that will enable the Board to make well-informed and well-educated decisions regarding the investment of Plan assets.

the following:

statement that properly reflects the Board’s tolerance for risk and that best 
helps the Board meet its rate-of-return, funded status and administrative 
expense objectives. 
 
 2. Asset Allocation Studies
 Conduct periodic asset allocation studies to determine whether or not the 
current asset allocation falls within the Board's investment objectives and 
guidelines. 
 3. Investment Manager Search 
 When deemed necessary, assist the Board in its due diligence and search for 
new investment manager(s) utilizing the appropriate data base. 
 4. Development of Investment Manager Performance 
 Standards/Guidelines
Assist the Board in the development and review of performance standards 
and guidelines with which the Board can measure each investment
manager's progress. Attend monthly meetings or special meetings as 
requested by the Board. 
 5. General Consulting Services
 Provide general consulting services as requested by the Board. These might 
include custodial search and selection, etc. 
 6. Performance Measurement & Monitoring
 Monitor the performance of the investment manager(s) to provide the Board 
with the ability to determine the manager’s progress toward achieving the 
Board’s investment objectives. Prepare and provide written quarterly 
reports submitted to the Board.

under Public Act 314 of 1965, as amended, with written quarterly reports 
submitted to the Board.

 Assist the Board in the development of an investment manager structure 
that provides adequate diversification with respect to the number and types 
of investment managers to be retained by the Board.

 Upon request, provide information regarding the holdings, sale and 
purchase of specific equities in order to complete proof of claims related to 
securities litigation.

to enter into an OCIO agreement.

experience in providing institutional investor consulting services.

employee retirement system with at least $250 million in assets.

the Investment Advisors Act of 1940.

investment fiduciary under Public Act 314 of 1965, as amended.

 City of Grand Rapids Retirement Systems 
 233 East Fulton, Suite 216 
 Grand Rapids, Michigan 49503

employee plans. The performance results should be based upon the period

be supplied to constitute an acceptable submission.

you.
